findings.summary: The subject correctly proves that every 23×23 sign-matrix determinant is divisible by 2^22. After normalizing the first row and column, row subtraction produces a 22×22 block −2B with B zero-one, so |det A|=2^22|det B|, including singular cases. Taking B=I_22 constructs a sign matrix with determinant 2^22, proving that 2^22 is the greatest universal divisor.

The subject establishes both directions of the sign/zero-one correspondence and hence D_23=2^22 max{|det B|: B∈{0,1}^{22×22}}. Every normalized sign matrix yields a zero-one core B, and every B yields A(B) with det A(B)=(−2)^22 det B. The examples B=0, B=I_22, and B=C⊕I_19 correctly give quotient values 0, 1, and −2, showing that all quotients do not occupy one residue class modulo any m>1 and that nonsingular examples have both parities.

The quotient examples rule out a universal nontrivial congruence restriction across all order-23 sign matrices, but they do not exclude additional congruence, Gram, or structural restrictions applying only to near-maximal determinants.

Combining the supplied real estimate D_23≤2^22·31,640,625√505 with 2^22 divisibility gives an integer quotient q≤⌊31,640,625√505⌋=711,034,613. The exact square comparisons certify this floor, and multiplication by 2^22 gives D_23≤2,982,295,321,444,352. This is exactly 186,421 below the ordinary integer floor 2,982,295,321,630,773.

The new endpoint is the strongest rounding obtainable solely from a common universal determinant divisor, because 2^22 is the greatest such divisor. It does not strengthen or rederive the underlying real analytic inequality, and it does not rule out stronger exclusions based on structural conditions specific to high-determinant matrices.

The supplied verifier is a reproducible exact replay artifact: it uses integer arithmetic and isqrt for the bound, checks endpoint multiplication and the ordinary floor exactly, deterministically generates the matrices from B=I_22 and B=C⊕I_19, and evaluates their determinants by integer Bareiss elimination with exact-divisibility checks.

The verifier is not an exhaustive test of all sign matrices, and no execution transcript is supplied. The universal divisibility statement rests on the symbolic proof rather than computation; the code supplies independently replayable consistency checks without floating-point or opaque computational dependence.

Together with the supplied published-record lower endpoint, the subject’s rounded upper bound supports the certified interval 2,779,447,296,000,000≤D_23≤2,982,295,321,444,352. No contradiction appears between the new upper-bound argument and the existing lower-record replay.

The supplied material does not determine D_23, prove that quotient 711,034,613 occurs as a zero-one determinant, show that the rounded upper endpoint is attainable, exclude that endpoint, classify candidate Gram matrices, or establish optimality of the published record.
The accepted contribution is an arithmetic upper-bound sharpening only. The subject exhibits no matrix exceeding the published lower endpoint and therefore supplies no new lower record.
